newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stals welcomes CME plan for S.African rand futures.
newsitem.headline: Stals welcomes CME plan for S.African rand futures.

text.p: South African Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Wednesday he welcomed plans by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) to trade futures and options on the South African rand.
The CME said on Monday it had filed for U.S. regulatory approval to trade the derivatives.
"It's a sign of South Africa's gradual integration into world financial markets," he told Reuters, adding it could also take some pressure off the forward cover market in South Africa.
The proposed CME contracts would be sized at 500,000 rand and would be quoted in U.S. dollars per rand.
The exchange said it plans to trade futures expiring in the March quarterly cycle, with settlement by physical delivery.
Quarterly and serial month options on rand futures contracts would also be offered. A start date will be set pending Commodity Futures Trading Commission approval.
